results.question: How many completed orders did each distribution center handle in 2024?
results.golden_sql: SELECT d.name AS distribution_center, COUNT(*) AS realized_orders FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` o JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` d ON o.distribution_center_id = d.id WHERE o.is_realized_order = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY realized_orders DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
  dc.name AS distribution_center,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders_count
FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` o
JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` dc
  ON o.distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE o.status = 'Complete'
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2024
GROUP BY dc.name
ORDER BY completed_orders_count DESC;
results.judge_reason: The ground truth filters on the business flag is_realized_order = TRUE, which likely covers more than status 'Complete' (probably everything except Cancelled and Returned). The generated query filters on status = 'Complete' only, so its counts would likely be lower than the expected ones.

results.question: Which product category made the most profit in 2024?
results.golden_sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.gross_margin_amount), 2) AS gross_margin FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_products` p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 1;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
  p.category AS product_category,
  SUM(CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC) - CAST(p.cost AS NUMERIC)) AS total_profit
FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi
JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_products` p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2024
  AND oi.status NOT IN ('Returned', 'Cancelled')
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY total_profit DESC
LIMIT 1;
results.judge_reason: Same tables, year filter and grain. Excluding Returned and Cancelled items matches the realized-revenue rule, and sale_price minus product cost is equivalent to gross margin, so the top category by profit should be the same.

results.question: Which distribution centers have the most orders with impossible shipping dates?
results.golden_sql: SELECT d.name AS distribution_center, COUNTIF(a.has_timeline_anomaly) AS anomaly_orders FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.int_order_attribution` a JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` o ON a.order_id = o.order_id JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` d ON o.distribution_center_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY anomaly_orders DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
  dc.id AS distribution_center_id,
  dc.name AS distribution_center_name,
  COUNT(o.order_id) AS impossible_shipping_order_count
FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` AS o
JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` AS dc
  ON o.distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE o.shipped_at IS NOT NULL
  AND o.shipped_at < o.created_at
GROUP BY
  dc.id,
  dc.name
ORDER BY
  impossible_shipping_order_count DESC;
results.judge_reason: The ground truth counts orders flagged by `has_timeline_anomaly` in `int_order_attribution`, which likely covers more than shipped-before-created (e.g. delivered before shipped). The generated query hand-rolls only `shipped_at < created_at` on `stg_orders`, so its counts and ranking can differ.

results.question: How much did each paying customer spend on average in 2023, by acquisition source?
results.golden_sql: SELECT u.acquisition_source, ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(oi.sale_price), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id)), 2) AS revenue_per_customer FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u ON oi.user_id = u.user_id WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2023 GROUP BY u.acquisition_source ORDER BY revenue_per_customer DESC;
results.generated_sql:
WITH user_spend_2023 AS (
  SELECT
    oi.user_id,
    u.acquisition_source,
    SUM(CAST(oi.sale_price AS NUMERIC)) AS total_spend
  FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi
  JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u
    ON oi.user_id = u.user_id
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2023
    AND oi.status NOT IN ('Returned', 'Cancelled')
  GROUP BY oi.user_id, u.acquisition_source
)
SELECT
  acquisition_source,
  COUNT(user_id) AS paying_customer_count,
  ROUND(AVG(total_spend), 2) AS avg_spend_per_paying_customer
FROM user_spend_2023
GROUP BY acquisition_source
ORDER BY avg_spend_per_paying_customer DESC;
results.judge_reason: Averaging per-user spend equals total revenue divided by distinct paying users, and the generated query uses the same tables, 2023 filter and grouping. results.question: How many website events did each traffic source generate in 2024, counting only activity after the user signed up?
results.golden_sql: SELECT oe.traffic_source, COUNT(*) AS events FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_online_events` oe JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u ON oe.user_id = u.user_id WHERE oe.created_at >= u.created_at AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oe.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY oe.traffic_source ORDER BY events DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
  oe.traffic_source,
  COUNT(*) AS total_events
FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_online_events` oe
JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u
  ON oe.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oe.created_at) = 2024
  AND oe.created_at >= u.created_at
GROUP BY oe.traffic_source
ORDER BY total_events DESC;
results.judge_reason: The generated query is logically identical to the ground truth: same tables, join on user_id, 2024 filter, post-signup filter (oe.created_at >= u.created_at), grouping by traffic_source, and ordering; only the column alias and predicate order differ.
